A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SOAR study. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–E are readable and support reliable matching across revisions and relocations.

before.justification: v1 reports original SOAR experiments on MATH and HARP, transfer evaluations on OlympiadBench, and extensive ablations and generated-question analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains these original results and adds SeRL comparisons, extended training controls, a question-correctness experiment, and an 8B-model evaluation.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 replaces its EMA recurrence with an explicit rolling-window mean for promotion. This is a local specification correction: v1 Section 4.2 already described averaging the most recent three steps, so an actual change in executed training is not established. The grounded objective, RLOO loops, and promotion mechanism otherwise remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same mathematical task coverage: MATH and HARP fail@128 training/evaluation and OlympiadBench transfer. The new model-size, training-duration, and filtered-question experiments remain within this coverage.

E2.justification: SeRL changes from a cited related method in v1 to an evaluated comparator on MATH and HARP in v3 Tables 4–5, with results at steps 50 and 100. The existing internal baselines and curated-data comparisons are retained.

E3.justification: v3 adds several distinct experimental settings: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct evaluation, HARP Hard-Only training extended from 1,500 to 6,500 steps, and training with 82 correct-only versus 144 well-posed PQ questions. SeRL uses fail@128 seed sets and evaluations at steps 50 and 100. These expand the evaluation design while retaining the original 3B protocols.

E4.justification: New analyses test whether longer direct training escapes the plateau (Figure 10), whether adding well-posed questions with incorrect answers helps (Appendix C.5, Figure 15), and whether benefits transfer to an 8B model (Appendix D.4). These substantially extend v1's evidence about compute, question quality, and model-size sensitivity.

E5.justification: The main metrics description changes from median and standard deviation to mean and standard deviation, resolving its inconsistency with v1 Appendix B.8 and the tables. New controls specify three seeds, and the 8B experiment specifies two teacher seeds with two students each. Existing repeated-run and bootstrap procedures are retained; increased runs for the original results are not established.

E6.justification: Existing numerical rows are retained, with equivalent rounding in Table 8. Substantial new results include SeRL step-100 pass@32 of 12.4% on MATH and 10.9% on HARP, quantified trained-teacher inference, and 8B Grounded-T versus Hard-Only results of 13.7% versus 9.1% pass@32. New curves report no benefit from extended Hard-Only training and improved performance after adding well-posed, incorrectly answered questions.

T1.justification: The bilevel objective and Proposition 1 on RLOO invariance under rejection sampling, including its assumptions and proof, are retained. No new theoretical result or substantive proof revision is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract narrows its reward-comparison claim from intrinsic reward schemes generally to intrinsic learnability rewards. The central claims about escaping plateaus, separating teaching from solving, and benefiting from questions with incorrect answers remain intact.

C2.justification: v3 interprets Appendix C.5 as evidence that correct answers and formatting alone do not explain gains. Appendix D.4 qualifies the larger-model evidence by reporting no promotions with reused hyperparameters. Table 1's caption also replaces conceptual-manifold expansion with the more restrained interpretation of diversity preservation relative to Intrinsic-T.

D1.justification: v3 adds SeRL configuration information, although it refers readers to the cited work for hyperparameter values, and states that the 8B experiment reuses the 3B hyperparameters without retuning. Algorithm 1 explicitly exposes the moving-average window and reward aggregation. Existing prompts, parsing instructions, hardware, and runtime disclosures are retained.

R1.justification: Sections 2 and A expand the discussion of intrinsic motivation and environment design, adding works such as Schmidhuber, Pathak, Colas, Prioritized Level Replay, and Deliberate Practice. They clarify SOAR's distinction from regret or learning-potential objectives. Numerous publication-metadata updates do not constitute new cited works or changed novelty claims.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, method exposition, and discussion undergo extensive condensation and rewriting. Related-work topics are reordered, standalone baseline and metric subsections are consolidated into evaluation, discussion paragraphs gain thematic organization, and an appendix contents list is added. These are substantial editorial changes beyond the added experiments.

P2.justification: v3 adds Figures 10, 15, and 18 and Table 9, expands Tables 4–5, and removes two illustrative questions from Figure 6. Table 1 and table captions are reformatted, and several displays are relocated. Most original plots are reused unchanged, preserving the overall visual organization.

improvement.justification: v3 strengthens the existing empirical case through an evaluated SeRL comparison, longer-training control, question-quality ablation, and larger-model check, while improving exposition and reporting consistency. The gains remain limited: Appendix C.5 changes dataset size alongside answer correctness, and the 8B experiment achieves no promotions. These additions improve support without fully resolving the mechanism and scalability limitations.
